walkthroughs.body_html:
Coronary heart disease is caused by narrowed coronary arteries.

Less O₂ reaches heart muscle. Risk factors: smoking, high-fat diet, lack of exercise, age.

Stents — physical fix, immediate, surgical risk. Statins — daily pills, lower cholesterol, side effects. Transplant — last resort, rejection risk.

asks you to evaluate — compare benefits and drawbacks.

1. Atria fill. 2. Atria contract, pushing blood into ventricles. 3. Ventricles contract, valves close (LUB-DUB), blood leaves via aorta and pulmonary artery.

Valves prevent backflow.

mcqs.q: Do all arteries carry oxygenated blood?
options: All arteries carry oxygenated blood and all veins carry deoxygenated blood.
No — the pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the heart to the lungs.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.

mcqs.q: Why does the left ventricle have a thicker muscular wall than the right?
options: Arteries and veins both carry the same mixed blood through the body.
The left ventricle is thicker because it is on the same side as the brain.
The left ventricle is thicker because it handles oxygenated blood, which is harder to pump.
It must pump blood at high pressure around the whole body; the right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs.

mcqs.q: In osmosis, which direction does water move?
options: Water moves towards the sugar because sugar attracts water molecules chemically.
From a region of higher water potential (less concentrated solution) to lower water potential.
Water moves from high solute concentration to low solute concentration.
